sentence: One vendor source claiming to be this telemetry is excluded: one post's title says 97,601 channels against its own body's 105,891 for what it presents as one 2019 cohort, no analyst or methodology is named, and its 8.8-year median lifespan is the age at death of channels that had already passed 10,000 subscribers [[youtube-channel-survival-rates-a-7-year-creator-study-creatormap]].
evidence: The cited note's body uses 97,601 consistently throughout (in title, headline, and every chart caption) with no instance of 105,891 anywhere, and contains no 8.8-year figure; the 105,891-vs-97,601 title/body mismatch and the 8.8-year median-lifespan claim belong to a different CreatorMap post ('YouTube Channel Lifespan: Half-Life Study of 97,601 Creators'), which the vault's own claims index records as the actual source of that discrepancy and figure.
suggested_fix: Swap the citation to note youtube-channel-lifespan-half-life-study-of-97601-creators-creatormap-creatormap, which documents the 105,891-vs-97,601 internal inconsistency and the 8.8-year median lifespan figure.

sentence: Four constraints travel with the October 2021 Twitch leak: 896,261 zero- or negative-revenue accounts were excluded before any percentile was computed, the unit is the account with production companies inside the top ranks, sponsorships and tips are excluded while the $100 payout floor censors the low tail, and no country composition is disclosed [[twitch-streamer-earnings-increase-for-top-gamers-data-from-hack-shows-wsj]] [[the-unbearable-lightness-of-streaming-superjoost-playlist]].
evidence: The van Dreunen SuperJoost Playlist note gives aggregate payout totals, the 25%-under-minimum-wage WaPo citation, the 3-women-in-top-100 fact, and revenue-mix percentages, but nowhere states the 896,261 zero-revenue exclusion, the $100 payout floor, that the unit is an account (with production companies among top ranks), or that country composition is undisclosed; all four of those specific constraints appear instead in the co-cited WSJ note's body.
suggested_fix: Drop this note as a citation for the sentence (or restrict its citation to the parts it actually supports, e.g. general leak commentary); the four enumerated constraints should cite the WSJ note only.

sentence: The much-repeated finding that 25% of the top 10,000 highest-paid streamers do not clear US minimum wage — the 8,000th-ranked account cumulating $29,396 since 2019, roughly $14,698 a year against a $15,080 federal minimum — therefore assumes US costs for a population of unknown nationality [[many-top-twitch-streamers-dont-make-minimum-wage-and-3-new-takeaways-from-the-tw]] [[twitch-responds-to-leak-revealing-earnings-of-top-streamers-and-more-dexerto]].
evidence: The Dexerto note's body covers only leak verification (mixed streamer responses), Twitch's official breach statement, the top-20 cumulative earnings table, and an internal Asmongold-figure inconsistency; it contains no mention of the 25% minimum-wage statistic, the 8,000th-ranked account, $29,396, $14,698, or $15,080 anywhere in its text.
suggested_fix: Cite only many-top-twitch-streamers-dont-make-minimum-wage-and-3-new-takeaways-from-the-tw for this sentence's numeric claims; drop the Dexerto citation here or move it to a sentence about leak-verification reliability.

sentence: Within-topic Patreon Gini rose from 0.30 in June 2013 to 0.60 by December 2020 across the complete transaction record, while cross-topic Gini fell from 0.80 to 0.72 [[quantifying-the-creator-economy-a-large-scale-analysis-of-patreon]]; VTuber between-creator Gini rose from 0.60 to 0.75 between 2018 and 2023 [[who-reaps-all-the-superchats-a-large-scale-analysis-of-income]]; and Pareto alpha fell across YouTube, Instagram, Facebook and Twitch between 2018 and 2024, n=104,719 [[rich-get-richer-platform-attention-and-earnings-inequality]].
evidence: The paper states the within-topic Gini coefficient 'has steadily and substantially increased from 0.30 in 2015 to 0.60 in December 2020' and the cross-topic Gini fell 'ever since mid-2015... from 0.80 to 0.72' -- both series are anchored to 2015 (Figure 13's axis begins at 2015), not June 2013, which is only the platform's launch date/full-dataset start, not the date the Gini was 0.30.
suggested_fix: Change 'rose from 0.30 in June 2013' to 'rose from 0.30 in 2015' and likewise anchor the cross-topic Gini's starting point to mid-2015, not June 2013.
